title: Reading the Participation Gap
transcript:
I expected students who lived near campus to play more sport, but the graph seems to show the opposite.
Before we explain that, how did you decide who counted as living nearby?
I used walking time. People in the nearest group could get to the main entrance in under fifteen minutes.
And what did respondents have to do to count as regular participants?
They had to report at least one session a week. I included activities outside university clubs as well.
Where did most of your responses come from? That might help explain the pattern.
Through team captains. They forwarded the link to players, including some who travel quite far for training.
That could explain the high rate among students who live further away.
So I'd describe the pattern in your sample and suggest using a general student mailing list for the next survey.

questions.prompt: The student grouped respondents by their ____ to the main campus entrance.
questions.explanation: 学生按走到校园主入口所需的时间给受访者分组。

questions.prompt: Regular participation meant reporting at least ____ of sport per week.
questions.explanation: 学生把每周至少参加一次体育活动作为定期参与的标准。

questions.prompt: The survey link was mainly forwarded by team ____.
questions.explanation: 学生说大部分答卷来自队长转发给队员的调查链接。

questions.prompt: How might the way the link was shared have affected the results?
options: It may have counted university club activities twice.
It may have brought in many active students who live far away.
It may have encouraged students near campus to report shorter journeys.
questions.answer: It may have brought in many active students who live far away.
questions.explanation: 有些收到链接的队员住得较远仍会来训练，这可能抬高了远住学生在样本中的参与率。

questions.prompt: How does the tutor suggest distributing the next survey?
options: Through a general student mailing list
Through instructors who run sports sessions
Through notices posted at training venues
questions.answer: Through a general student mailing list
questions.explanation: 导师建议下一次通过面向全体学生的邮件名单发放问卷。
